text: tlh-gui is a GUI for The Last Harness built as a standalone copy of get-bb/bb, deliberately not a GitHub fork. Diego wants it to stay relatively close to upstream so it keeps benefiting from bb's ongoing development: keep fork deltas small and inventoried, and leave upstream identity and behavior alone unless a delta is explicitly approved.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The repo is public on purpose (Diego, 2026-10-06). Public repos get unlimited free standard GitHub-hosted runners, which replace upstream's paid Blacksmith runners for fork CI, and the desktop auto-updater fetches release metadata from GitHub release assets without auth, which only works on a public repo. Making it private would break both.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Diego intends to eventually fork bb's mobile app (apps/mobile) too. Until then apps/mobile, its upstream mobile workflows (disabled in repo settings), and the in-app links to bb's TestFlight/APK stay exactly as upstream ships them; repoint them when the mobile fork happens rather than hiding them now.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Diego decided (2026-10-06) that tlh-gui launches `tlh` by default for the Pi provider, with no silent fallback to plain `pi` when tlh is missing (show not-installed with TLH install guidance instead). BB_PI_BRIDGE_COMMAND still overrides; any non-tlh command keeps upstream's npm install/update behavior. Install/Update buttons must work with TLH: install runs TLH's release install.sh, update runs `tlh update`. On 2026-10-08 Diego approved renaming the provider's display label from 'Pi' to 'TLH'; the internal provider id 'pi' must not change because threads persist it.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: tlh --version reports the private Pi runtime version, not TLH's, so tlh-gui cannot use it for the TLH version. Diego first approved reading <agent-dir>/tlh/install-state.json as a stopgap (2026-10-07), tracked as diegopetrucci/the-last-harness#746. That shipped in TLH v0.45.0 as tlh version --json (schemaVersion 1). On 2026-10-14 tlh-gui switched to it, and Diego approved keeping the install-state.json + tlh --version fallback. The fallback covers older TLH and remote custom package sources, where tlh version exits 1. Always pass --json: on older TLH, plain tlh version is treated as a model prompt.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Session storage: on 2026-10-07 Diego decided to keep tlh-gui (bb) Pi sessions and tlh CLI sessions separate; no shared layout and no code to make them talk. bb keeps its own --session-dir (~/.bb/pi-bridge-sessions, flat <threadId>.jsonl, which bb needs for fork/checkpoint/discard); TLH keeps <agent-dir>/sessions/--<cwd>--/. A shared-layout design (option 3) was considered and dropped because it would only be one-way and would add concurrent-writer and transcript-drift risks. Future intent: write a skill, shipped in both the bb fork and the tlh CLI, that teaches each agent how to access the other's sessions. Useful fact for that skill: Pi's picker accepts any .jsonl name, and 'tlh -r --session-dir ~/.bb/pi-bridge-sessions' filters by each file's header cwd, so it can already list GUI threads for the current folder. The separate skill-roots follow-up is tracked in its own entry.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Telemetry in tlh-gui is deferred on purpose. Diego wants to replace upstream bb's PostHog telemetry with TelemetryDeck, matching how The Last Harness does it (see the-last-harness docs/telemetry.md), instead of just hiding or defaulting off the in-app 'Share anonymous usage data' switch. Until then telemetry stays off by default because no PostHog key ships.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Skill-list fix for tlh mode was investigated on 2026-10-07 and Diego postponed it. What was observed: bb always merges the static ~/.pi/agent/skills root, which tlh never loads, so the GUI offers skills tlh doesn't know. A live 'tlh --mode rpc --no-session' answering get_commands reported 20 loaded skills from TLH packages (git/npm under the TLH agent dir), ~/.agents/skills, and ~/.claude/skills/synced, which a TLH extension adds at runtime. bb's filesystem scan can't see package or extension-added skills, even upstream. Options on the table: (A) re-implement Pi package skill discovery from settings.json, which misses extension-added skills and drifts; (B) in tlh mode, have host.ts ask tlh via get_commands (~1.1s cold start) with a cache keyed on settings/install-state, and move ~/.pi/agent/skills from the static declaration to resolved roots in non-tlh mode. B was recommended; no decision taken.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Diego's guidance (2026-10-08) for removing upstream features in tlh-gui: keep the original bb code in place to make upstream intake easier. Instead of deleting code, find the most 'root' switch that removes, disables or hides a feature, such as a plugin registry or bundle list, a default setting, a declaration flag, or a build/package include list, and change only that, with the delta recorded in docs/tlh/patch-inventory.md. Delete upstream files only when no such root switch exists, and ask first.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: On 2026-10-12 Diego said he would like back-and-forth session sync between tlh-gui and the tlh CLI, then deferred it ('we can do this later'). This revises the 2026-10-07 'keep separate' intent in the related entry. Options weighed: (1) GUI->CLI handoff via 'tlh --session ~/.bb/pi-bridge-sessions/pi_<uuid>.jsonl' (works today; GUI thread must be idle; CLI turns never show in the GUI because the GUI renders from ~/.bb/bb.db, not the session file); (2) one-off CLI->GUI import that rebuilds bb.db history (medium fork delta); (3) live two-way mirror (large, fragile: concurrent writers, transcript translation, lasting upstream drift). Recommendation given: start with (1), add (2) if needed, avoid (3). Still open: handoff vs live mirror, and which direction matters most.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: On 2026-10-13 Diego set the tlh-gui product direction that users should stop caring about branch management: they start a new chat and that's it (captured in VISION.md). Concretely, a new chat defaults to a new git worktree on desktop and mobile (same web composer). He chose 'default only': users can still pick Project checkout or Reuse existing, and an explicit pick stays remembered per project per device as upstream does. Rejected alternative: forcing Worktree on every new chat (picks applying to one chat only), because users must still be able to choose and it would be a larger, drift-prone change in the composer hook. He also asked that gnosis entries always be committed together with the changes they relate to.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Observed 2026-10-13 on Diego's Mac, two tlh-gui test failures are environment-only and unrelated to code changes (both pass in tlh CI): (1) apps/app UpdatePluginDialog.test.tsx asserts the en-US string 'Failed on Jul 22, 2026.' but the machine locale is en_GB (renders '22 Jul 2026'); run @bb/app tests with LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 LANG=en_US.UTF-8 to match CI. (2) packages/scripts test/ci-performance.test.mjs runs pnpm in a temp dir outside the repo's pnpm@9.15.0 packageManager pin, so it picks up the global Homebrew pnpm 12.x, which rejects --fetch-retries; vitest --exclude did not skip it via turbo, so rely on CI for that file. Node tooling also needs the prefix: env -u PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR mise exec node@22.19.0 --.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Diego decided (2026-10-15) that tlh-gui shows only the TLH provider (provider-pi, which launches tlh) by default, superseding the earlier 'TLH plus Claude Code' set. Claude Code is now disabled by default like Codex and ACP (Cursor, opencode, etc.) via defaultEnabled:false in the bundled plugin registry; nothing is deleted and each can still be re-enabled in plugin settings. provider-usage stays enabled because it is a usage dashboard, not an agent provider. The 'Pi' display label stays 'TLH' and the provider id 'pi' must stay.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Decision (Diego, 2026-10-15): the bb thread composer shows a second muted line for TLH threads with only 'fast' and subscription usage, mirroring the TLH terminal footer. Usage is published by TLH itself in RPC mode via ctx.ui.setStatus('tlh-usage', <formatted segment>), and bb forwards allowlisted Pi setStatus keys (fast, tlh-usage) as provider-pi extension state. Rejected: having bb's provider-pi plugin fetch subscription usage itself by reading TLH auth.json OAuth tokens (duplicates credential/refresh and weekly-visibility logic). Other TLH footer items (agent name, cost, cwd, git status/PR, MCP statuses) were explicitly out of scope; other providers are not a concern for this fork.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>
